Static signed projection convergence does not determine an arbitrary lift’s penalty.

literal_edits.source_excerpt: **M4. Partial homogeneity and zero crossing.** Retain all Assumptions 3.4: Ω=R×Θ, Φ(w,θ)=wφ(θ), V(w,θ)=|w|Vtilde(θ), bounded differentiable φ,Vtilde with Lipschitz differential; convex R and its original derivative bounds; Sard-type regularity for each g_f; either Θ=R^(d−1) with uniform C1 spherical limit g_f(rθ) whose limit has dense regular values, or bounded closed convex Θ with the stated Neumann conditions for every relevant g_f. Verify the Neumann branch makes the constrained tangential field equal the source field and preserves the boundary. Prove the C.4/C.5 escape estimates, then the signed-projection stationarity argument with explicit positive/negative parts (C.6). For unfavorable negative-w support use the C.18 trajectory reparametrization: while w≤0 and q=|θ−θ0| is small, w'≥η/2 and q'≤−w(ε+Lq); hence crossing time is at most 2M/η, and ε chosen proportional to r0/(exp(LM²/η)−1) controls q. The printed bound 2/η without M is not a uniform bound for arbitrary w0∈[−M,0]. Prove actual hitting at some time ≤T, not the generally false assertion w(T)=0 for one common fixed T for all w0.
literal_edits.replacement: **M4. Partial homogeneity and zero crossing.** Retain all Assumptions 3.4 together with the full inherited Assumptions 2.1: Ω=R×Θ, Φ(w,θ)=wφ(θ), V(w,θ)=|w|W(θ), bounded differentiable φ,W with Lipschitz differential, convex R and its original derivative bounds. Make the source quantifier explicit: the Sard and boundary clauses apply for all f in the Hilbert space (in particular f=0), either Θ=R^(d−1) with uniform C1 spherical limit whose limit has dense regular values, or bounded closed convex Θ with C1 boundary and Neumann G_f for all f. Do not silently replace all f by realized risk gradients. Prove the direct all-endpoint energy and radial second-moment identities for every definition-level flow, without adding bounded initial weights to stationarity or escape. Signed narrow convergence gives norm moments; radial S'=−2(<f,m>+P) gives S=O(t). Failure of either Jordan-part stationarity forces action at least c/(1+t), contradicting finite total dissipation. The full global semiconvexity of |w|W makes W convex by positive-w slices; boundedness and the applicable boundary premise then make W constant. This is a derived consequence of the full hypotheses, not a new constant-penalty assumption. Prove the reflected sign dynamics, robust negative-level trapping, and positive-action escape in both domain branches. At infinity normalize by k=r², prove the compactified fields are uniformly close using the all-f C1 assumption and uniform boundedness, and prove Lyapunov decay through closed boundary-contact time sets before an Arzelà–Ascoli perturbation argument. Do not infer AC from continuity of the compactified energy. Use universal reversed-forcing trapping to clear the unfavorable branch after a finite M/b wait, choosing the forcing neighborhood before t0 and M. The scalar C.18 inequalities still give individual hitting by 2M/η and their proved displacement estimate; the printed 2/η and a common exact hitting time for every w0∈[−M,0] are not valid. Source Assumptions3.4 alone do not imply the advertised global semiconvexity; record the smooth Neumann counterexample honestly, while retaining the full approved library assumptions.

literal_edits.source_excerpt: **M5. Conditional conclusions and examples.** Prove the C.16/C.17 contradiction: separating support forces positive mass into an invariant negative sublevel, while convergence of the prescribed projection would keep the flow permanently inside a neighborhood that the escape lemma forces it to leave. Carry the W2-flow convergence assumption in Theorems 3.3/3.5 or the explicitly proved projected weak-convergence replacement. Prove F(μ_t)→F* in the corresponding topology; prove the retained particle/time qualitative limit interchange by monotone energies plus finite-time G6 convergence. No unconditional time convergence, finite-m rate or finite-width SGD global-optimum claim is permitted. On the examples companion verify signed-square ReLU regularity and its exact data/integrability/Sard premises locally before using it as a theorem example; the classical ReLU coordinate map fails the differentiability premise. Failure of separation is a boundary example, not a converse global-optimality theorem.
